description: Food-logs data access layer, per-date query keys, read/write TanStack Query hooks, and the PURE summarize math. This is the foundation the form (FEAT-002) and dashboard (FEAT-003) build on. Mirror the macro-goals feature structure exactly. Before running the full suite, materialize src/features/energy/domain from main (see context.verification_instructions) and REMOVE it before finishing; the NEW food-logs tests must NOT import @energy.
steps: Create apps/macros-web/src/features/food-logs/types.ts: export FoodLog = Database['public']['Tables']['food_logs']['Row']; export AddFoodLogInput derived from the food_logs Insert type (Omit server-managed 'id','created_at','updated_at'; keep user_id, name, calories required; quantity/unit/logged_on/protein_g/fat_g/carbs_g optional as per Insert). Import Database from ../../data/database.types. No any.

Create apps/macros-web/src/features/food-logs/queryKeys.ts: export const foodLogKeys = Object.freeze({ daily: (userId: string | null | undefined, date: string | null | undefined) => ['food-logs','daily', userId, date] as const }); keyed by BOTH userId AND date so invalidation is precise per date. Mirror macro-goals/queryKeys.ts doc style.

Create apps/macros-web/src/features/food-logs/foodLogs.data.ts following macroGoals.data.ts: type Client = SupabaseClient<Database>; a private toClearError('food-logs: <context>', error) that returns new Error(`food-logs: ${context}`, { cause: error }) and NEVER interpolates the raw error into the message. export async getDailyFoodLogs(client, userId, date): queries .from('food_logs').select('*').eq('user_id', userId).eq('logged_on', date).order('created_at', { ascending: true }); on error throw toClearError('failed to load the daily food logs', error); return data ?? []. export async addFoodLog(client, input: AddFoodLogInput): never mutate input; build a fresh insert object applying documented defaults for required columns the user form omits — quantity defaults to 1 and unit defaults to 'serving' (document this choice in a comment: the manual form captures per-serving macro totals, so quantity=1 serving keeps the CHECK (quantity > 0) satisfied without asking the user); .from('food_logs').insert({...}).select().single(); on error throw toClearError('failed to add the food log', error); return data. Keep functions < 50 lines.

Create apps/macros-web/src/features/food-logs/summarizeDailyMacros.ts: a PURE, React-free module. Define metric type (calories/protein/fat/carbs). export function summarizeDailyMacros(logs: readonly FoodLog[], goal: MacroGoal | null) returning { consumed: {calories,protein,fat,carbs}, remaining: {...}, percent: {...} }. consumed = immutable reduce over logs summing calories, protein_g, fat_g, carbs_g (no mutation; start from a frozen zero object, return a new accumulator each step). Map goal metrics: calories<-calorie_target, protein<-protein_g, fat<-fat_g, carbs<-carbs_g; when goal is null treat each target as 0. remaining = target - consumed per metric (MAY be negative — do NOT clamp remaining). percent = target > 0 ? clamp(consumed/target*100, 0, 100) : 0 (bar percent ALWAYS clamped to [0,100]). Round sensibly for display but keep the pure values precise. Add a tiny clamp helper. Export a hasGoal boolean or let callers check goal === null. No any; functions < 50 lines; freeze any shared constant.

Create apps/macros-web/src/features/food-logs/useDailyFoodLogs.ts: useQuery({ queryKey: foodLogKeys.daily(userId, date), queryFn: () => getDailyFoodLogs(getSupabaseClient(), userId as string, date as string), enabled: Boolean(userId) && Boolean(date) }); return UseQueryResult<FoodLog[], Error>. Mirror useMacroGoal.ts.

Create apps/macros-web/src/features/food-logs/useAddFoodLog.ts: useAddFoodLog(userId) using useMutation({ mutationFn: (input: AddFoodLogInput) => addFoodLog(getSupabaseClient(), input), onSuccess: (saved) => queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: foodLogKeys.daily(userId, saved.logged_on) }) }). Invalidate by the INSERTED row's logged_on so the correct per-date query refreshes. Return UseMutationResult<FoodLog, Error, AddFoodLogInput>. Mirror useSaveMacroGoal.ts.

Add tests under apps/macros-web/src/features/food-logs/__tests__/: foodLogs.data.test.ts (mock the .from().select().eq().eq().order() chain for getDailyFoodLogs success + empty + error-non-leak; mock .from().insert().select().single() for addFoodLog success + error-non-leak + does-not-mutate-input + applies quantity=1/unit='serving' defaults). Mirror macroGoals.data.test.ts incl. a RAW_DETAIL leak assertion. summarizeDailyMacros.test.ts (empty logs -> zero consumed, remaining==targets, percent 0; partial; exactly-at-goal -> remaining 0, percent 100; over-goal -> remaining negative, percent clamped 100; null goal -> targets 0, no NaN). useDailyFoodLogs.test.tsx (loading->success->error via QueryClient wrapper; idle/disabled when userId or date missing). useAddFoodLog.test.tsx (isPending->success; invalidateQueries spy called with foodLogKeys.daily(userId, saved.logged_on); not called on reject). Mirror the existing wrapper/spy patterns. Tests must be self-contained (no @energy).
acceptance_criteria: apps/macros-web/src/features/food-logs/ contains types.ts, queryKeys.ts, foodLogs.data.ts, summarizeDailyMacros.ts, useDailyFoodLogs.ts, useAddFoodLog.ts and a __tests__ folder.
getDailyFoodLogs scopes by user_id AND logged_on and returns [] (never null) on empty; addFoodLog never mutates its input and applies quantity=1 / unit='serving' defaults.
Error messages from the data layer contain only the stable 'food-logs: ...' context and never the raw Postgrest message/details/hint (asserted in tests).
summarizeDailyMacros is pure: remaining can be negative, percent is clamped to [0,100], null goal yields 0 targets and no NaN.
useAddFoodLog.onSuccess invalidates exactly foodLogKeys.daily(userId, saved.logged_on) (asserted by spy).
npx vitest run passes (with energy domain temporarily materialized); npm run typecheck and npm run lint pass with zero any and no console usage.
verification: cd apps/macros-web && materialize energy domain, then: npx vitest run src/features/food-logs && npm run typecheck && npm run lint
Confirm new food-logs test files do not import @energy (grep).
findings: Implemented the food-logs foundation under apps/macros-web/src/features/food-logs/ mirroring macro-goals: types.ts, queryKeys.ts (foodLogKeys.daily keyed by userId AND date, frozen), foodLogs.data.ts (toClearError non-leaky wrapper; getDailyFoodLogs scoped by user_id+logged_on ordered by created_at, returns [] never null; addFoodLog builds a fresh insert object with quantity=1/unit='serving' defaults, never mutates input), summarizeDailyMacros.ts (pure, frozen ZERO_TOTALS seed, immutable reduce, remaining may be negative, percent clamped [0,100], null goal => 0 targets no NaN), useDailyFoodLogs.ts (useQuery enabled only when userId AND date), useAddFoodLog.ts (useMutation invalidating foodLogKeys.daily(userId, saved.logged_on)). DEVIATION FROM PLAN: the hand-written food_logs Insert type marks `quantity: number` as REQUIRED (not optional as the plan assumed), so AddFoodLogInput = Omit<Insert,'id'|'created_at'|'updated_at'|'quantity'> & { quantity?: number } to relax it; data layer uses input.quantity ?? 1 / input.unit ?? 'serving' so an explicit undefined cannot clobber the default. 20 new tests all pass. Full suite 176/176 green with the energy domain temporarily materialized at /projects/sandbox/APP/src (removed before commit, never staged). typecheck (tsc --noEmit) and lint (eslint, no-console) both clean. New tests contain no @energy import (grep verified).
